incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Articles 1-10, 20-22, 58-60, 62-63, 210-212)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) and provincial Registro Mercantil where the registered office is located
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (Deed of Incorporation) filed via the electronic portal of the Colegio de Registradores
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of €3,000 (approx. USD 3,250) fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in-kind at incorporation; funds must be deposited in a Spanish bank account (certificate of deposit required) and remain blocked until registration
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the company is duly incorporated under the name [Company Name] S.L. with registered office at [Address]. That the share capital of €3,000 is fully subscribed and paid up as per the bank certificate. That the following officers are appointed: [Name] as Sole Administrator, [Name] as Secretary. That the registered office is adopted as the legal seat for all purposes. That the Administrator is authorized to execute all filings, registrations, and licenses necessary for the company's operations, including environmental permits for the sewage treatment plant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain NIE (Foreigner Identification Number) for all non-resident incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oficina de Extranjería (Immigration Office) or Spanish Consulate in the country of residence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form EX-15, passport copy, and proof of no criminal record. For EU nationals, NIE is issued directly; for non-EU, require visa if applicable. The NIE is mandatory for any shareholder or director who is not a Spanish resident.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If application is rejected, appeal within 1 month to the Delegación de Gobierno or reapply with corrected documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open provisional bank account and deposit share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish bank (e.g., Banco Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank) with commercial registry compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the draft deed of incorporation, NIE numbers, and passport copies. Deposit the minimum capital of €3,000. Obtain a bank certificate (certificado de depósito) stating the amount and account holder. The account must be blocked until the company is registered.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses due to AML concerns, provide additional source-of-funds documentation or choose another bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute and notarize the deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notario) in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All incorporators must appear before the notary, either in person or via power of attorney. The notary will verify identity, capital deposit certificate, and the articles of association (estatutos). The deed is signed and the notary issues a certified copy (copia autorizada) for registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, correct the articles and resubmit. If the deed is rejected, the notary will provide a written explanation and a new appointment can be made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for provisional tax identification number (CIF provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – local tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified copy of the deed to the AEAT within 30 days of notarization. Use Form 036 (Censo de empresarios). The provisional CIF is issued immediately, valid for 6 months until final registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, provide additional documentation as requested by the AEAT officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company with the Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Registro Mercantil corresponding to the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified copy of the deed, Form 036, and payment of registration fees. The registry reviews the deed for legal compliance. Once approved, the company is legally incorporated and the registration is published in the BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil).
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect (defecto), correct the deed via a public deed of rectification and resubmit within the given period (usually 15 days).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain definitive CIF and register with local authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, return to AEAT with the registration certificate to obtain the definitive CIF. Simultaneously, apply for the municipal operating license (licencia de actividad) and register the company with the local social security office (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social) for employer registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal license is delayed, request a provisional license or file an appeal with the Ayuntamiento.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Medio Ambiente of the Autonomous Community (e.g., Junta de Andalucía, Generalitat de Catalunya) – Dirección General de Calidad Ambiental
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización Ambiental Integrada (AAI) – Integrated Environmental Authorization, plus specific water discharge permit (Autorización de Vertido)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) – Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report (Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Ordinaria) – Category A, as the plant exceeds 100,000 population equivalent (p.e.) or treats hazardous waste
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Directive 91/271/EEC (Urban Wastewater Treatment) and Spanish Royal Decree 509/1996: BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, Suspended Solids ≤ 35 mg/L, Total Nitrogen ≤ 10 mg/L (for sensitive areas), Total Phosphorus ≤ 1 mg/L. Air emissions: VOC limits per EU Directive 2010/75/EU (IED) – typically ≤ 20 mg/Nm³ for non-methane VOCs. Sludge handling must meet Directive 86/278/EEC on sewage sludge.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Certificado de Protección Contra Incendios) from the local fire department, structural load inspection (Inspección Técnica de Edificios) for all buildings, and workplace safety clearance (Plan de Seguridad y Salud) approved by the labor authority (Inspección de Trabajo).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident or newly incorporated foreign entity obtaining taxable status in Spain must apply for a NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) for legal entities and, if engaging in taxable operations, obtain a VAT registration number. The procedure is performed by filing Form 036 or Form 037 (simplified) through the AEAT electronic registry. The entity must provide: certificate of incorporation, articles of association, proof of identity of the legal representative, and a Power of Attorney appointing a tax representative resident in Spain if the entity does not have a permanent establishment but makes taxable supplies. For entities with establishment, the NIF is granted on incorporation and simultaneously used for VAT. Submission is online via digital certificate or a Spanish fiscal representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is a resident company subject to Corporate Income Tax (IS) at the general 25% rate on worldwide income. The SL has separate legal personality; its members are not taxed on undistributed profits. Spain applies a territorial scope for non-resident entities without establishment (only Spanish-source income taxed) but the SL, being incorporated in Spain, is fully resident and taxed on global income. Tax exempt zones (e.g., Canary Islands ZEC) have limited application, but standard SL entities are outside such special zones unless specifically registered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not apply 'check-the-box' classification. Eligible elections include: (1) Consolidated tax group election for groups under common control (Art. 64-67 LIS), allowing offsetting profits/losses across group members at 25%; (2) Patent box regime election (Art. 23 LIS) – 60% exemption of qualifying intellectual property income; (3) Special tax regime for qualifying holding companies (ETVE, Art. 21, 22 LIS) – election for participation exemptions on foreign dividends and capital gains; (4) Hybrid mismatch elections – Spain implements ATAD (Directive (EU) 2016/1164) and requires neutralizing hybrid mismatches; no positive election is available, but entities may adjust treatment under anti-hybrid rules; (5) Option for installment of Corporate Income Tax based on prior-year taxable base is available but not an entity-classification election. Standard SL cannot elect pass-through status; only certain small entities (Sociedades Civiles) may opt, not SLs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 – No general registration threshold applies to established entities; any entity performing business activities as defined under Art. 5 LIVA must register for VAT from the first taxable supply. Non-established foreign entities must register for VAT before the first taxable transaction regardless of volume. Certain small businesses eligible for the simplified regime (régimen simplificado) have annual turnover thresholds of EUR 250,000 for invoicing and EUR 250,000 for purchases, but this regime is optional and not a threshold for exemption from registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain is implementing e-invoicing mandates under the 'Crea y Crece' Law (Ley 18/2022). From 2023, all entrepreneurs and self-employed must issue electronic invoices when dealing with other businesses (B2B). Private electronic invoicing solutions must comply with AEAT technical specifications, including the 'Verifactu' system (Royal Decree 1007/2023) requiring software to produce a digital bill of lading with cryptographic hash, QR code, and immediate deliverability to AEAT in real time. Large companies (turnover > EUR 6 million) are obliged to use the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) – a real-time VAT reporting system sending transaction details to AEAT within 8 calendar days of issue, using XSD/API web-service specifications. For non-large taxpayers, real-time clearance is not mandatory but will become mandatory when Crea y Crece regulations are fully adopted (expected by 2025); until then, electronic invoicing is mandatory but filing may be periodic (monthly/quarterly). Digital stamping by AEAT is not currently used for standard invoices; authentication is via the Verifactu 'QR + hash' and secure communication channels.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating (0% VAT) applies to: (1) dispatches of goods to third countries/destinations outside the EU (Art. 21 LIVA) – including direct exports by the seller, indirect exports via consignment, and transfers to authorized warehousekeepers; (2) transport services directly linked to export goods; (3) supplementary services such as loading, unloading, and similar; (4) certain services related to imported goods under customs duties suspension; (5) services provided to non-resident customers relating to movable tangible property transported outside Spain (Art. 70 LIVA). Eligibility requires the exporter to hold the goods for export, receive consideration from a non-resident, and physically ship goods out of the EU within the legally established period (typically 90 days for transport). For EPC contracts (reverse osmosis water treatment works), the design, commissioning, and technical services physically performed in Spain to be delivered remotely or used outside Spain may be zero-rated if the recipient is a non-resident business without establishment in Spain under the place-of-supply rules (Art. 69 LIVA).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA – Documento Único Administrativo) or Summary Declaration (REX-based statement) showing the goods have left EU customs territory
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill, or CMR (road transport) evidencing physical dispatch and delivery to destination outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Cobro al Exterior) or SWIFT MT103/MT202 payment instruction confirming foreign currency consideration received
Commercial Invoice with explicit indication of 0% VAT and the export clause
Proof of Intra-EU or third-country customs transit, if applicable (T1/T2 or NCTS)
Export declaration acceptance receipt from AEAT (e.g., 'Documento de Acompañamiento al Exportador' – DAE)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT conducts export verification and cross-matching with customs data. If zero-rating is wrongly claimed: (1) the VAT becomes due at the Spanish standard rate (21%) plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%/yr); (2) the taxpayer may be liable for a mild sanction (50% of the amount due) if incorrect disclosure, or severe sanction (100%-150%) if fraudulent manipulation of invoices or false documentation; (3) criminal liability (Tax Fraud) may arise if the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 – imprisonment of 1 to 5 years plus fines up to 6 times the fraud amount; (4) retrospective clawback extends to 4 years of assessments, but 10 years in cases of tax crime; (5) the taxpayer loses the refund claim for the export period. Under the SII, electronic reporting makes discrepancies immediately detectable; failure to produce the full documentation bundle within the 180-day deadline triggers a mandatory rebuttal presumption of non-export and immediate assessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as the national central bank, monetary authority and prudential banking supervisor; the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCOM) of the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio, Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa, as the competent authority for foreign exchange regulation, foreign investment control and capital-movement surveillance; with ancillary AML/CFT supervisory powers vested in SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención de Blanqueo de Capitales y Delitos Monetarios).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a euro-area member and the EUR is fully and unconditionally convertible on both current and capital account. Current-account operations, including trade settlements, service fees, contract milestone payments, interest, dividends and profit remittances by an ES-SL to foreign shareholders, are free from exchange-control authorization, surrender requirements, conversion ratios or quantitative ceilings. Capital-account operations are liberalized under Articles 63 and 65 TFEU, Law 20/2003 on Foreign Investment and Royal Decree 571/2023; however, non-EU/EFTA investments into so-called critical infrastructure, which includes municipal water supply and sewage treatment networks, may trigger either a post-investment declaration or, where the investor is directly or indirectly controlled by a third-country government or public body or where the non-EU private investment exceeds EUR 500 million, a prior authorization requirement. Since the entity is an operational EPC vehicle for sewage treatment and reverse-osmosis water works, the treasury blueprint requires an upfront determination of the ultimate beneficial-owner nationality to confirm whether prior clearance under Royal Decree-Law 8/2020-Law 19/2021 continuity rules applies. Profit remittance is subject only to a statutory 19% dividend withholding tax for non-resident shareholders, reduced to 0% for EU corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and to applicable double-tax-treaty rates (commonly 5-15%) for treaty residents; no foreign-exchange or administrative hurdles exist beyond the standard withholding and Beneficial Ownership certification documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no surrender, mandatory conversion, or retention-period requirement on export proceeds or foreign-currency receipts; the ES-SL may freely hold export and contract proceeds in EUR or in any convertible currency in resident or foreign-currency accounts. The only operative obligations are statistical and documentary: (i) any receipt from non-residents exceeding EUR 50,000 per transaction must be declared to the Banco de España through the Balance-of-Payments statistical declaration entered on the quarterly settlement record; (ii) the underlying invoice and FIDIC/EPC contract documentation must evidence the commercial reality of each inbound wire to prevent AML misfiling; (iii) non-resident payments denominated in foreign currency are recorded for AEAT customs and tax audit purposes; and (iv) there is no ratio, timeline or conversion formula mandating repatriation to EUR. Export-credit collections from municipal clients in Spain are domestic payments and require only VAT invoicing and the statutory withholding, if any.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (EUR/USD) + Operational EUR Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A. (BBVA) (SWIFT BBVAESMM)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR Account + USD collection account for World Bank escrow disbursements
Operational EUR Account + Escrow segregation account for municipal contract performance bonds
Operational EUR Account for EPC subcontractor settlements
Operational EUR Account + supplementary USD clearing account for Latin American counterparties

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for auxiliary and perimeter treasury uses, LOW for primary escrow and capital-account rails. Spanish payment institutions and electronic money institutions operate under the PSD2 regime implemented by Royal Decree-Law 19/2017 and Law 16/2009; a foreign digital EMI, including a UK or Latin American fintech, must hold a Spanish or EU/EEA licence with passporting rights or act as an appointed agent of a Spanish-licensed payment institution. Structural legal constraints: an EMI may not take deposits or grant credit; client funds must be safeguarded in segregated accounts at a credit institution; EMIs generally lack direct SWIFT membership, full correspondent banking networks and the institutional rating required to interface with World Bank escrow structures. Consequently, the ES-SL treasury may deploy an EMI only for low-value operational expenses, foreign payroll and travel settlement, while all capital injections, escrow receipts, LC operations and export-proceeds collection must be cleared through a Tier-1 commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of the legal representatives and signatories is de facto mandatory at Tier-1 Spanish banks for a non-resident-held ES-SL; remote video-identification is rarely permitted for foreign corporate entities and is accepted only at bank discretion. The standard compliant alternative is a notarial power-of-attorney executed by each director and legalized/apostilled, together with the deed of incorporation, appointing a local apoderado (attorney-in-fact) who must physically attend the bank interview bearing a valid DNI or NIE. All non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners are expected to hold a Spanish NIE (foreigner identification number). Under Law 10/2010 on AML/CFT, the bank must complete identification of the company, its directors and UBOs before onboarding; in practice the interview is also used to verify the source of funds, the intended transaction profile and the opinion on the FIDIC/World Bank contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: non-resident ultimate beneficial owners arranged through a chain of trusts or intermediaries with no visible Spanish economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and sworn-translated deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución), current shareholding register, UBO declaration filed with the Spanish Commercial Registry, full NIE and passport copies of each UBO, audited financial statements of the immediate parent, group structure chart, lease agreement for the Spanish registered office, payroll and social-security registration evidence, and a written substance statement confirming where the EPC project management and operational decisions are taken.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: source of wealth for the foreign equity injection unclear, with incoming wires originating from jurisdictions perceived as high-risk or tax-favoured.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements of the contributing shareholder, foreign tax residence certificates for the last three years, the notarized capital-increase resolution and deed showing cash disbursement, CRS/FATCA self-certifications, signed AML source-of-funds questionnaire, and a comprehensive explanation of the accumulated funds with supporting asset or business income documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: regulated water/sewage treatment activity presented without the required statutory licence, municipal concession or environmental permits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid administrative concession from the municipal authority, integrated environmental authorisation (Autorización Ambiental Integrada) or applicable water-discharge permit, the signed FIDIC Yellow Book contract, the World Bank procurement reference or grant agreement, construction-all-risks and professional-indemnity insurance certificates, and the telecom/monitoring compliance certificate for the reverse-osmosis plant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: front-loaded or milestone-concentrated USD wire activity from the World Bank escrow account misread as structuring or round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury-flow dossier containing the escrow agreement, engineer-issued milestone certificates matched to the payment schedule, back-to-back purchase orders and supplier invoices, a cash-flow forecast by quarter, an auditor's reconciliation letter, and a written statement confirming that no funds are returned to the non-resident shareholder outside the capital-reduction or dividend process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: planned payments to equipment suppliers or subcontractors located in Latin American countries subject to sanctions exposure or high AML risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-clearance sanctions screening reports (UN, EU and OFAC lists) for all counterparties, World-Check and negative-media results for UBOs, end-user and end-use certification for the reverse-osmosis works, local in-country customer-due-diligence files of the Spanish bank's correspondent, and a legal opinion confirming that the transactions arise from a World Bank-financed public-works contract.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound routing protocol: the foreign shareholder effects the capital contribution by SWIFT MT103 REMIT or, for high-value cover arrangements, MT202 COV; ordering customer is the non-resident investor, beneficiary is the ES-SL (NIF) with IBAN format ES##-XXXX-XXXX-CCCC-CCCC-CCCC and the beneficiary bank BIC. Field 70 remittance information must state the purpose as 'FDI capital increase - foreign direct investment under Law 20/2003' and cite the notarial deed reference; the wire must be preceded by the notarized capital-increase deed recorded in the Commercial Registry so that the bank can classify the entry. For any receipt equal to or exceeding EUR 50,000, the ES-SL must file the quarterly balance-of-payments statistical declaration with the Banco de España; for a non-EU/EFTA shareholder, a post-investment declaration to the DGCOM Register of Foreign Investments is due within one month after the disbursement, and if the shareholder is third-country state-controlled or the amount exceeds EUR 500 million, prior authorization must be obtained before the wire is accepted. The receiving bank will verify the UBO declaration update and may place a temporary hold pending receipt of the notarial deed. Where the World Bank escrow denominates in USD, the preferred route is a USD technical account at BBVA or Santander (New York) receiving the escrow release by MT103, followed by an immediate FX forward conversion into EUR at the same institution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and settlement rails: (i) EUR payments to EU/EEA suppliers via SEPA Credit Transfer (1 business day) and TARGET2 for high-value EUR wires; (ii) non-EU and USD payments via SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary bank's USD correspondent and a designated intermediary bank, including full purpose text in field 70, invoice references and the underlying project contract number to avoid AML delays; (iii) for high-value electromechanical equipment procurement, commercial letters of credit under ICC UCP 600, including transferable LCs where the municipal client or World Bank opens a confirmed LC in favour of the ES-SL and the ES-SL instructs the advising bank to transfer part of the proceeds to the equipment manufacturer; (iv) standby letters of credit and performance/advance-payment bonds issued by the Spanish relationship bank to guarantee EPC milestones; and (v) ancillary intra-group cash-pooling sweeps to concentrate surplus EUR in the operational account. All outbound wires must map to underlying invoices, FIDIC milestone certificates and, where applicable, customs declarations to support the commercial-substance test and Spain's reverse-charge VAT rules for cross-border supplies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright FX forwards with a Spanish or EU-licensed credit institution under ISDA 1992/2002 documentation and EMIR reporting for non-financial counterparties below the clearing threshold
EUR/USD FX swaps and tom-next rollovers to manage the timing of World Bank escrow releases against EUR operational funding requirements

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in Latin American currencies with restricted convertibility (e.g., Argentine peso, Venezuelan bolívar) to hedge project-revenue exposure without physical settlement in the restricted currency, settlement being made only in USD or EUR with fully licensed counterparties

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) to transform USD-denominated escrow receivables into EUR liabilities or synthetic EUR funding, subject to IFRS 9 hedge accounting designation and ISDA collateral arrangements

European-style FX options and zero-cost collars for protecting minimum revenue conversion rates under the public-works contract, purchased on a non-speculative basis and governed by the corporate treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Deposito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (via Electronic Deposition platform of Registro Mercantil Central)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved by the shareholders' meeting within 6 months after fiscal year-end; deposit must be filed within 1 month of approval. For a 31 December fiscal year-end: approval by 30 June and deposit by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers closure of the company's registry sheet ('cierre registral'), preventing any other corporate registration until the accounts are deposited; ICAC may impose administrative fines generally ranging from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 for failure to deposit; persistent non-compliance may give rise to dissolution and liquidation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades - Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the close of the 6-month post-year-end period. For a 31 December fiscal year-end: 1-25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers late-payment surcharges and default interest; penalties under the General Tax Law may be up to 100-150 percent of the tax due, with forced collection measures and suspension of tax-compliance certificates for public contracts and subsidies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Summary Return (Declaracion-Resumen Anual de IVA - Modelo 390)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 1-30 January following the end of the calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing gives rise to late-payment surcharge plus interest; failure to submit an accurate informative return generally attracts a penalty of EUR 200, increased for obstruction or material omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Third-Party Transaction Report (Declaracion de Operaciones con Terceras Personas - Modelo 347)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during February (1-28 February, or 29 February in leap years) for transactions exceeding EUR 3,005.06 with any third party or subsidies exceeding EUR 300.51.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission penalty starting at EUR 200; proportional penalties apply to omitted transactions; persistent failure may be treated as serious tax-infringement conduct.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Mandatory Legalization of Corporate and Accounting Books (Legalizacion de Libros Obligatorios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, by 30 April of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-legalized books cannot be used as evidence in commercial litigation; the registry may reject subsequent filings, and responsible officers may incur liability under the Commercial Code and audit sanction regimes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Confirmation Attached to Annual Accounts (Declaracion de Titulares Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (attachment to annual accounts deposit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual accounts deposit; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, by 31 July. Changes in UBO between deposits must be reported within 1 month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incorrect or incomplete UBO information exposes the SL and its managers to fines under Law 10/2010 on Money Laundering, generally up to EUR 60,000 for minor infringements and up to EUR 150,000 for serious infringements; registry closure may apply until corrected.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit is required if, for two consecutive years, the SL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: total assets exceeding EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover exceeding EUR 5,700,000; average headcount exceeding 50 employees. Auditing is also compulsory where required by shareholders holding at least 5 percent of capital, by court or registry order, or by project-finance and public-works concession agreements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP under the Plan General de Contabilidad (PGC), aligned with EU-adopted IFRS; SMEs and micro-entities may use the simplified PGC Pymes / PGC Microempresas; consolidated groups may apply IFRS-EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain an on-site UBO register ('Libro Registro de Titulares Reales') and update it contemporaneously with any share transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership. A current UBO declaration is confirmed annually as part of the annual accounts deposit; interim transfers must be notified to the Registro Mercantil within one month. The annual confirmation covers all shareholders, indirect holdings, and entities on the UBO chain and certifies that no unrecorded changes occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro Registro de Socios (Register of Members)
Libro de Actas de la Junta y del Organo de Administracion (Minute Book of shareholder and director meetings)
Libro Registro de Titulares Reales (Ultimate Beneficial Owner Register)
Libro de Contabilidad (accounting books and inventory/annual accounts records)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - USD 450 per year for standard Spanish registered office and registered agent services; higher in Madrid and Barcelona for enhanced compliance support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 5,000 per year for a small-to-medium SL; fees increase with group consolidation, municipal concession complexity, and external funding requirements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate in the first profitable tax period and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory eligibility conditions. Small entities may qualify for reduced rates under applicable annual tax legislation. Deductibility restrictions, including interest limitation, participation exemption rules, capitalization requirements, and tax-credit ceilings, may materially affect the effective rate. Tax credits may apply for qualifying research and development, technological innovation, audiovisual production, and certain investment activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic headquarters using a digital certificate, Cl@ve where available, or an authorized representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the ordinary filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the final day is not a business day, the deadline extends under the applicable administrative-calendar rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number, registered office, tax period, legal form, activity classification, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish NIF where the entity is Spanish tax resident. A non-resident company filing only on Spanish permanent-establishment or Spanish-source income must use the applicable non-resident identification and permanent-establishment details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting assets, liabilities, equity, turnover, expenses, accounting profit or loss, and reconciliation items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A permanent establishment must report attributable Spanish business assets, liabilities, income, and expenses on a functionally separate basis, supported by books and allocation records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary differences between accounting profit and taxable profit, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation adjustments, impairment, interest limitation, and related-party adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign activity unless attributable to a Spanish permanent establishment or otherwise taxable in Spain. Apply treaty relief only after confirming residence, beneficial ownership, and income characterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use of tax losses generated in prior periods, subject to utilization limits and anti-abuse rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses legally attributable to the Spanish taxpayer or Spanish permanent establishment may be claimed. Maintain origin-period schedules and evidence that no prohibited change of ownership or activity manipulation occurred.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base, applicable rate, gross tax liability, deductions, credits, withholding tax, installment payments, and final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign withholding credits or treaty-based relief only where statutory documentation, limitation rules, and income-source requirements are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions, restructuring, tax incentives, hybrid arrangements, tax losses, and other mandatory disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile disclosures with transfer-pricing documentation, intercompany agreements, customs records, withholding returns, and the financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payment reference, direct-debit mandate where available, electronic signature, representative authority, and filing receipt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain the AEAT filing receipt, payment confirmation, digital certificate logs, and representative authorization for the statutory audit period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Voluntary late filing without prior AEAT notice generally attracts a surcharge of 1% plus an additional 1% for each full month of delay during the first 12 months. After 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest from the end of that 12-month period. If AEAT initiates proceedings, penalties for an underpaid tax liability may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount, subject to aggravating or mitigating factors. Interest applies to late payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Corporate Income Tax installment-payment return, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly installment periods, generally April, October, and December
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ordinary filing periods are the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. Electronic payment by direct debit normally requires an earlier cutoff established by AEAT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, tax period, tax year, and installment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident files only where Spanish corporate tax installment obligations arise, including through a Spanish permanent establishment or another taxable Spanish presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax-liability method or current-period taxable-base method, depending on the taxpayer's statutory status and election.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the applicable method against the prior Modelo 200, current-period accounting data, and any consolidated-tax treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Percentage applied to the relevant tax base or prior-year liability, reduced by eligible deductions and prior payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude income not legally attributable to the Spanish taxpayer or permanent establishment and preserve allocation calculations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable, NRC or payment reference, direct-debit information, and electronic signature.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile each installment with the final Modelo 200 and record any overpayment or shortfall.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment may generate surcharges, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties. Underpayment caused by an incorrect installment calculation may result in tax assessment and penalties where culpability is established.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, related-party transaction and tax-haven information return, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual filing month is November.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, tax period, and filing reason.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Spanish corporate taxpayers and Spanish permanent establishments must assess filing obligations separately from the residence of the related counterparty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Counterparty, relationship type, transaction category, aggregate amount, valuation method, and income or expense classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border financing, services, royalties, construction or engineering support, procurement, guarantees, and other related-party dealings when thresholds are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of transactions exceeding applicable category and counterparty thresholds, including specific requirements for the same transaction type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile amounts to the general ledger, invoices, contracts, withholding filings, and transfer-pricing local-file schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions involving jurisdictions treated as non-cooperative or tax-haven jurisdictions and certain restructurings or transfers of business assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the current Spanish jurisdiction list and anti-abuse rules rather than relying solely on the counterparty's formal residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or materially incorrect disclosure may trigger formal-information penalties and, where the omission conceals an underpayment, additional tax-adjustment and tax-fraud penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 220, consolidated Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters where the Spanish tax-consolidation regime applies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally follows the Modelo 200 deadline for the consolidated tax group.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Parent entity, tax group number, group perimeter, tax period, and subsidiaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent may participate only through structures expressly permitted by Spanish group-tax rules and must satisfy ownership, voting, and filing requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregation of each group member's accounting result, tax adjustments, tax losses, deductions, and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only entities validly within the group and maintain separate-company calculations for audit and exit-from-group purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Elimination of intragroup income and expenses, deferred taxation, intragroup dividends, and other consolidation adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border items remain subject to source, withholding, transfer-pricing, and permanent-establishment analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Consolidated tax base, rate, credits, installments, and amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm joint and several exposure of group members and the effect of restructuring, insolvency, or departure from the group.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: The group parent is primarily responsible for consolidated filing. Incorrect consolidation, omitted group members, or unpaid tax can generate assessments, interest, penalties, and subsidiary liability for responsible entities or persons.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% generally on dividends paid by a Spanish company to a non-resident. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply where statutory ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, anti-abuse, and beneficial-ownership conditions are satisfied. The Spain-resident recipient exemption regime may apply to qualifying Spanish recipients.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Spanish payer normally applies the domestic rate unless a reduced treaty rate or exemption is properly supported. Obtain a valid tax-residence certificate issued by the recipient's tax authority, verify beneficial ownership and limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test requirements where applicable, collect any required forms or declarations, and retain ownership, holding-period, substance, and subject-to-tax evidence. If excess withholding is imposed, the recipient may seek a refund from AEAT using the applicable non-resident tax refund procedure. Treaty relief does not override Spanish anti-abuse, beneficial-ownership, or anti-conduit rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Spanish rates are generally 19% for interest and 24% for royalties paid to non-residents, with a 19% rate generally applicable to qualifying EU/EEA recipients under the relevant statutory rules. A treaty may reduce the rate, commonly to 0%, 5%, 8%, 10%, or 15%, depending on the treaty and income type. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may provide an exemption for qualifying associated EU companies, subject to legal-form, minimum-participation, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse conditions. Spanish-source rules, permanent-establishment attribution, treaty residence, and beneficial ownership must be assessed separately.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is generally not required for transactions with the same related party that do not exceed EUR 250,000 in the relevant transaction category during the tax period, provided statutory conditions are met. Master File obligations generally apply to Spanish entities or groups forming part of a qualifying multinational group, including where consolidated group turnover is at least EUR 45 million. Simplified documentation may apply to entities below the applicable turnover threshold, but it does not eliminate the arm's-length requirement.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations filing regime. Substance is nevertheless central to Spanish anti-abuse analysis, beneficial-ownership determinations, treaty access, EU directive exemptions, permanent-establishment risk, corporate-residence analysis, controlled foreign company rules, hybrid-mismatch rules, and the general anti-abuse rule. A Spanish SL should maintain genuine decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity under effective control, premises or operational infrastructure appropriate to its functions, risk assumption, financial capacity, contemporaneous contracts, and demonstrable commercial rationale. A municipal sewage or water-treatment EPC business should separately document tender activity, engineering supervision, procurement, project management, commissioning functions, warranty obligations, and allocation of construction-site risks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of Spanish-source income, fabricated costs, false invoices, unreported permanent-establishment activity, manipulated project margins, or deliberate use of false transfer-pricing records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, in addition to tax and interest. Tax fraud involving an amount exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax period may constitute a criminal offence, generally punishable by imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded, subject to aggravated-offence rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face civil and tax subsidiary liability where they negligently or intentionally fail to prevent the breach, plus criminal liability where personally involved. Criminal conviction may lead to disqualification from public office or subsidies, asset seizure, restitution, and other judicial measures. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be imposed by a court in appropriate criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False accounting, commercial-document fraud, and invoice fabrication
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creation or use of fictitious supplier invoices, sham subcontracting, circular payments, concealment of related-party beneficiaries, or accounting entries designed to inflate deductible EPC costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, denial of deductions or credits, late-payment interest, administrative penalties, and potential criminal liability for falsification, fraud, or accounting offences under the Spanish Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, finance officers, and signatories may incur criminal liability, fines, civil restitution, professional disqualification, and joint or subsidiary liability for unpaid tax where statutory conditions are satisfied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length engineering fees, procurement mark-ups, shareholder loans, guarantees, royalties, management charges, or profit allocations unsupported by functions, assets, risks, or reliable comparables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may make a primary adjustment, impose compensating or secondary adjustments, deny deductions, recharacterize payments, apply withholding tax, and impose documentation or tax-underpayment penalties. Related-party transactions may also trigger Modelo 232 failures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face subsidiary tax liability and civil claims where they knowingly approve abusive arrangements or fail to maintain required books and documentation. Criminal liability requires the applicable elements of a tax, accounting, or fraud offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Performing design, construction supervision, commissioning, installation, or project-management activities in Spain without registering or filing for a Spanish permanent establishment where a treaty or domestic rule creates one.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of Spanish corporate tax on attributable profits, payroll and indirect-tax consequences, withholding exposure, interest, and administrative penalties. Treaty construction-site duration thresholds must be assessed under the applicable treaty and facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and project managers may be liable for deliberate concealment, failure to register, or obstruction. Courts may impose criminal measures only where the conduct satisfies the relevant criminal offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding-tax failure and treaty-abuse conduit arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payment of dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees without withholding, reliance on an invalid residence certificate, conduit-company routing, treaty shopping, or failure to verify beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish payer may owe the unwithheld tax, interest, and withholding-related penalties. Treaty or EU-directive relief may be denied under beneficial-ownership, principal-purpose, anti-abuse, or subject-to-tax rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and authorized signatories may incur subsidiary liability for willful or negligent failure to withhold and may face criminal exposure if the arrangement forms part of a fraudulent tax scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared cash, corruption, procurement fraud, and public-contract misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Kickbacks, hidden commissions, bid manipulation, off-book payments, inflated change orders, payments to public officials or intermediaries, or diversion of municipal-project funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential criminal prosecution for bribery, corruption, fraud, embezzlement, money laundering, or public-procurement offences; consequences may include imprisonment, fines, confiscation, debarment from public contracts, exclusion from subsidies, tax reassessment, and dissolution or judicial intervention in severe cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers may be personally prosecuted. Civil restitution, confiscation, disqualification, precautionary asset freezes, and court-ordered travel restrictions may apply. Corporate criminal liability may arise where the company lacked effective compliance controls or benefited from the offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify beneficial owners, inadequate customer or supplier due diligence, unexplained escrow or SWIFT flows, sanctions evasion, suspicious transactions not reported, or inadequate record retention.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish Law 10/2010, serious and very serious breaches may attract significant administrative fines, potential publication, temporary prohibition from conducting business, and responsible-manager sanctions. Criminal money-laundering liability may include imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and corporate penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers, directors, beneficial owners, and managers may be personally sanctioned or prosecuted where they participated in, authorized, or recklessly enabled the conduct. Asset freezing, confiscation, and judicial travel restrictions may be available in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate-shell, beneficial-owner concealment, and nominee arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of a dormant Spanish SL with no operational capacity, nominee directors, undisclosed ultimate owners, circular ownership, sham subcontractors, or a company established solely to obtain treaty or procurement benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax benefits, treaty relief, deductions, or legal standing for the relevant arrangement; tax reassessment; administrative penalties; contract termination; and potential criminal liability for fraud, money laundering, false documentation, or tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face veil-piercing claims, civil restitution, subsidiary tax liability, confiscation, disqualification, and criminal imprisonment where the arrangement is used to commit or conceal an offence. Travel bans are court-imposed and fact-dependent, not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain Spanish accounting records, destruction of source documents, refusal to provide AEAT information, inconsistent VAT and corporate-tax ledgers, or obstruction of a tax inspection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Formal-accounting and information penalties, estimated assessment, denial of deductions, late-payment interest, tax-underpayment penalties, and possible criminal consequences for obstruction or document falsification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for negligent or deliberate obstruction, failure to preserve records, or misuse of corporate assets. Courts may impose fines, disqualification, restitution, asset measures, and travel restrictions in criminal cases.
